newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares edge up, Handelsbanken leads.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares edge up, Handelsbanken leads.

text.p: Swedish shares edged up in light summer trade volumes, lifted by gains in telecoms group Ericsson and commercial bank Handelsbanken.
At 1020 GMT the general index was up 0.35 percent at 3,167.96 in turnover totalling 1.13 billion crowns.
Ericsson rose 2.5 crowns to 362 and fellow blue-chip, drug company Astra was unchanged at 143 crowns.
Handelsbanken led rises, up 2.4 percent or six crowns to 253 crowns, on a correction, a dealer said.
"Handelsbanken, like other shares, is recovering losses from yesterday," a dealer said.
Bar code reading systems maker Pricer rose 9.5 crowns to 290.5, 3.3 percent.
"(Swedish business daily) Dagens Industri wrote something about a positive buy signal and the market has reacted a lot on this in a dearth of other news," a broker said.
Market players were waiting for U.S. unemployment figures due at 1230 GMT. The data was expected to confirm non-inflationary U.S. economy.
Vehicle maker Volvo rose one to 214.5 crowns after selling its stake in Renault for a capital gain of 750 million crowns on Thursday.
